fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Children are active and curious, and bumps, falls and sporting knocks are a normal part of growing up. When a dental injury or sudden toothache happens, it can be upsetting for both children and parents. At Precision Dental, we provide calm, gentle urgent care for children and clear guidance for families.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is a Children's Dental Emergency?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A children's dental emergency is any injury or problem affecting a child's teeth, gums or mouth that causes pain, bleeding, swelling or damage. Common examples include:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A knocked-out, loose or displaced baby or adult tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A chipped or broken tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Toothache or swelling, which may indicate infection

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Cuts to the lips, tongue or gums

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Something stuck between the teeth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Caring for baby teeth and adult teeth after an injury differs in important ways, so it is always worth calling us for advice.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: When to Seek Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Call us as soon as possible if your child has:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A knocked-out adult tooth, which needs care within 30 minutes

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A knocked-out or pushed-in baby tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A broken tooth or visible pink or red spot in the centre of a broken tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Toothache, facial swelling or fever

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A tooth that has changed colour after an injury

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Call 000 or go to your nearest hospital emergency department if your child has a head injury, has lost consciousness, has swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, or bleeding that will not stop.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Stay calm and reassure your child. Rinse their mouth gently with water and apply pressure to any bleeding with clean gauze. A cold compress can help with swelling.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Knocked-out baby tooth: do not put it back in. Keep it and contact us for advice.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Knocked-out adult tooth: hold it by the crown, rinse briefly in milk if dirty, and replant it if possible, or store it in milk. Call us immediately. Our knocked-out tooth page has more detail.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Broken tooth: keep any fragments in milk and bring them with you.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Give pain relief suitable for your child's age and weight as directed on the packaging.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We greet your child warmly and move at a pace that feels comfortable for them. We gently examine the injured area and take digital X-rays if needed to check the roots and developing adult teeth. We explain our findings to you and your child in simple terms. Treatment depends on the injury and may include smoothing or repairing a broken tooth, splinting a replanted adult tooth, treating infection or managing soft tissue injuries. Our goal is to relieve discomfort and protect developing teeth.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Offer soft foods for a few days and help your child keep the area clean with gentle brushing. Watch for colour changes, swelling or pain over the following weeks, as some injuries show effects later. Follow-up visits allow us to monitor healing and the development of adult teeth. For sport, a custom mouthguard helps protect growing smiles.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Children's Dental Emergencies

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Children's Dental Emergencies

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Our team takes a gentle, reassuring approach with children and involves parents in every decision. We also provide ongoing children's dentistry, so your child can return to a familiar place for follow-up care.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Should I put my child's baby tooth back in?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Replanting a baby tooth can damage the developing adult tooth. Contact us for advice.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How do I know if it is a baby tooth or an adult tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Children usually have baby teeth until around age six, when adult teeth start coming through. If you are unsure, treat it as an adult tooth and call us immediately.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: My child's tooth turned grey after a fall. What does that mean?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Discolouration can indicate that the nerve has been affected. Please book an assessment so we can monitor the tooth.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can you see my child on the same day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We keep time available for urgent care and will do our best to see your child on the day you call.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What if my child is too upset to be examined?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We never force treatment. We take things slowly, and if needed, we focus on comfort first and plan care for when your child feels calmer.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How can I help prevent dental injuries?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A custom mouthguard for sport, supervision during play and safe car seats all help reduce the risk of dental injuries.
